newsitem.title: FRANCE: France plans talks to change pension fund law.
newsitem.headline: France plans talks to change pension fund law.

text.p: French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn said on Tuesday he wanted to hold early talks on changing the pension fund law passed earlier this year when the previous centre-right government was in power.
"It will be necessary to modify the text" to respond to criticism when it was passed, he said.
He told a conference that he wanted to ensure that "we are neither in the situation of the previous law, nor taking a step backwards."
"The question is to know whether a complementary pension savings scheme can have a place in our country without putting universal schemes in danger," Strauss-Kahn said at the Europlace conference.
"It will be in this spirit and one of collective negotiations that the 1997 law will be changed," he said.

When the Socialists and Communists were in opposition, they criticised the legislation creating volontary private pension funds, arguing that incentives for employers -- including exemptions from social security charges -- would drain money from social security funds.
